PROCUREMENT

Value Engineering Below Ground: Ask What Changes and What Stays Required

Evaluate alternatives against the complete project outcome.

In this insight

Define the objective before seeking savingsDescribe the alternative completelyExamine evidence and uncertaintyRecord the accepted changeFor your project discussionDiscuss a project ↗

Educational overview · Project-specific design and execution require qualified review.

Define the objective before seeking savings

A value-engineering exercise should begin with the required performance, interfaces and delivery constraints. Clarify whether the objective is lower cost, a simpler sequence, less site occupation or another measurable benefit. Without that baseline, an alternative may look attractive because it quietly removes an obligation. The responsible designers must determine whether the revised proposal remains suitable for the project.

Describe the alternative completely

Ask for the technical basis, scope changes, affected interfaces and programme implications. Include what additional work other parties would need to undertake. A reduction in one package may create cost elsewhere. Present the comparison on a whole-project basis so the decision is not driven by a saving that exists only within one contractor’s quotation.

Examine evidence and uncertainty

Identify which benefits are demonstrated and which are assumptions awaiting confirmation. Request relevant supporting information and a clear review route. Do not treat a preliminary sketch as an approved construction solution. Where more investigation or design work is required, include its cost and timing in the evaluation rather than ignoring it in the headline saving.

Record the accepted change

If the alternative is approved, update drawings, specifications, responsibilities, programme and commercial documents. Retain the decision rationale and any conditions attached to acceptance. Brief affected teams so the old and new approaches are not mixed in delivery. Properly controlled value engineering improves the project outcome while preserving a clear account of what was changed and why.

For your project discussion

Use these questions to structure a conversation with the project’s qualified design and delivery team. This article is general procurement guidance, not a site-specific design, method statement or compliance assessment. The cited international resources provide background; applicable local requirements and the approved project documents govern the work.

Take this into your next conversation

  • Set the required outcome before comparing alternatives.
  • Evaluate costs across affected packages.
  • Implement approved changes through all project records.
